subject: 🛠️ Anthropic Claude adds Docs, Slides & Design — no app-switching
intro: Two big moves dropped yesterday, and they rhyme more than they look. Anthropic ships a full productivity suite inside Claude. OpenAI publishes a bug tracker for when its models go rogue. One lab is racing to own your workflow. The other is quietly admitting its models hide mistakes and forge data. Both moves are about trust, just from opposite directions. Meanwhile, DeepMind cuts AI search costs by 162x. The efficiency era is here whether the safety one is or not.

news.headline: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork, adds Docs, Slides, and Design tools
news.body: Claude just merged its chat and background work modes into one. No more switching between tools. Here's what changed: you drop a task, close your laptop, and Claude keeps working. If it hits a wall, it asks you. You stay in control, it handles the grind. The bigger news is three new tools now live in beta on all paid plans: The part worth getting excited about: you can go from one-pager to deck to matching visual, all inside one chat. No copy-pasting between apps. If you used Cowork before, your chats, projects, and files are still there. Rolling out to Pro and Max plans soon.
bullets: Claude Docs - write and edit documents, fix lines yourself or leave comments for Claude to handle
Claude Slides - build decks, move elements around, then present straight from Claude or export normally
Claude Design - mock up visuals without leaving the conversation

news.headline: Google DeepMind's self-improving agent cuts AI search costs by up to 162x
news.body: Google DeepMind just showed an AI that gets better at solving hard problems by learning from its own past attempts. That's the core idea behind Dream-RSI . Here's the problem it solves. When an AI explores a complex problem, it uses a strategy to decide where to look next. Most systems use a fixed strategy that never improves. Updating it live is expensive. Dream-RSI found a clever middle path. Instead of running new expensive experiments to test better strategies, it replays old ones. Think of it like a coach reviewing game footage instead of running a whole new practice. The AI simulates thousands of alternative approaches using its history, picks the best, then deploys it for real. That last point matters. You can drop this on top of any existing AI agent without retraining it. It just makes the search smarter over time.
bullets: Works across algorithm design, math optimization, and GPU engineering
Cuts AI calls by up to 162x in some settings
Does not change the underlying model, only how it explores

news.headline: Free open-source tool turns a photo and audio into a minutes-long talking avatar video
news.body: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 just dropped, and it does something that used to cost serious money: give it a photo and an audio clip, and it spits out a realistic talking-head video. No studio. No camera. No subscription fee. It's fully open source under the MIT license , meaning you can use it commercially, modify it, and ship it in your own products. Here's what makes it actually usable: To get started: git clone the repo, set up a conda environment, and run torchrun with your image and audio inputs. Weights download straight from Hugging Face. This opens the door to AI presenters, dubbed content, and virtual characters built entirely from code.
bullets: Generates videos in just 8 inference steps , roughly 15x faster than older approaches, about 1 minute for a 10-second clip
Handles long videos without the face drifting or lips falling out of sync
Supports multi-person scenes where two characters talk to each other
Works on real humans, anime, and animals
